section_map.summary: The title and summary identify Five Models for China's Water Scarcity and the 2013-2025 decision horizon.
The summary compresses three scarcity mechanisms, five sub-problems, headline forecasts, transfer routes, and the AHP-neural evaluation.
The introduction connects China's population and freshwater imbalance to demand growth, floods, pollution, and the thirteen-year strategy request.
The nomenclature binds regional demand, supply, resources, population, GDP, pressure, reservoir, transfer, desalination, pollution, and efficiency symbols.
Model-one assumptions hold policy, economic growth, and climate changes steady while later models specify geographic, cost, and recovery assumptions.
Statistical Yearbook series, province tables, watershed indicators, COD data, and strategy attributes are turned into model inputs.
Function fitting, grey correlation, Verhulst dynamics, CV storage economics, and water-pressure definitions establish the quantitative core.
Correlation, least-squares estimation, reservoir screening, geographic feasibility, objective optimization, and minimum spanning tree steps are ordered explicitly.
Forecast tables, province priorities, six transfer routes, desalination timing, pollution rankings, water-saving classes, and strategy scores are reported.
The paper compares fitting alternatives, forecast residuals, pressure and CV rankings, desalination cost timing, and indicator classes.
The authors credit quantitative forecasting, multiple fitting methods, indicator quantification, pollution urgency grading, and AHP-neural evaluation.
The source acknowledges limited forecasting data, simplifying restrictions, and missing exact pollution-control benefits.
The conclusions connect model-specific outputs to validity, feasibility, cost efficiency, and a combined strategy evaluation.
The government position paper turns transfer, storage, and pollution rankings into a concise leadership action sequence.
References provide desalination, groundwater, maps, neural-network, and statistical-yearbook context while leaving computational provenance incomplete.
The appendix supplies MATLAB for regression, function fitting, Gray Model (1,1), association analysis, and plotting outputs.

assumptions.summary: Population, policy, economic growth, and climate are held sufficiently stable for the thirteen-year forecast.
Historical statistical series are adequate inputs for fitting and grey prediction.
Short-term total resources are represented by surface and groundwater, with groundwater omitted from the storage decision.
CV is a useful volatility indicator and reservoir cost and capacity can be represented with simplified functions.
Province coordinates, watershed attributes, and terrace attributes are adequate for transfer feasibility.
Coastal demand grows linearly and at most two desalination plants are built during 2013-2025.
Annual sewage emissions remain within environmental self-recovery and treatment cost rises with COD.
Water consumption per unit GDP beta is a useful water-saving urgency indicator.
AHP impact attributes and selected quality labels can train a neural evaluation interface.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: The summary states three China water problems and five sub-problems for a 2013-2025 strategy.
Yearbook water-use observations span 1997-2010 and include total, industrial, agricultural, and live consumption.
The fit table reports linear and power functions with SSE, R-square, adjusted R-square, and RMSE.
Grey correlation uses total water consumption as x0 and agricultural, industrial, and live consumption as factor sequences.
Verhulst prediction reaches 6770.1 hundred million cubic meters in 2025 in the printed table.
The reservoir table ranks CV, pressure, cost, capacity, and benefit for Chinese provinces.
The national transfer network assigns edge weight w=1/eta and displays six optimal routes.
The desalination section reports epsilon=5 as reasonable and derives a 13-year benefit ratio of 5.889.
The watershed table ranks pollution-control demand, with Hai highest and Southwest lowest.
The water-saving classification gives national beta0=0.0255 and regional beta values.
The AHP-neural table uses four strategy attributes and quality labels from 1 to 10.
Appendix code imports 97-10data.txt, 00-10 water supply.txt, and B_Data.txt.

models.summary: Collect 1997-2010 consumption and socioeconomic series, fit alternatives, test, then forecast 2013-2025.
Normalize reference and factor sequences, calculate coefficient terms, and average them into associate degrees.
Accumulate the original series, build B and Y, estimate a and b, generate the time response, reduce it, and inspect residuals.
Compute surface-water CV, combine capacity and construction cost, and prioritize provinces with need and economic benefit.
Assign watershed and terrace attributes, compute route distances and benefits, remove infeasible edges, and build a minimum spanning tree.
Forecast coastal demand, constrain two plants, express declining unit cost, and minimize total cost over the second build time.
Grade watershed pressure and quality, select the most urgent watershed, then rank cities by COD and upstream effects.
Divide beta, water consumption per unit GDP, into five classes and compare it with water-supply pressure.
Build hierarchy and judgment matrices, check consistency, encode four attributes, and classify strategy quality from 1 to 10.
Translate route, storage, and pollution rankings into inter-watershed and within-watershed action recommendations.
Import named data files, run regressions, fit functions, execute Gray Model (1,1), calculate association, and plot diagnostics.
Fit alternatives to Yearbook water-use data and test their forecast table.
Rank socioeconomic factors by association with total water consumption.
Estimate and test the non-monotonic grey forecast before predicting 2013-2025.
Screen volatile and economically justified provinces for storage projects.
Construct feasible local and national transfer routes using distance, benefit, and MST.
Choose two-plant scale and timing for a coastal city under declining cost.
Rank watershed and city pollution-control demand and optimize COD reductions.
Classify water-saving need through unit-GDP consumption beta.
Check impact matrices and derive a coherent multi-criteria strategy weighting.
Map AHP attributes to a 1-10 strategy quality output.

results_trace.summary: Function fitting forecasts 2025 water use between 6878.65 and 7028.3 hundred million cubic meters depending on fit.
The Verhulst table forecasts 6770.1 in 2025, while nearby prose says 7039 and compares a government ceiling of 7000.
CV and cost-benefit screening highlights Henan, Liaoning, Heilongjiang, Anhui, Hubei, Zhejiang, Fujian, and Jiangxi for storage attention.
The transfer model selects six national routes and identifies Yangtze-to-Yellow/Hai direction in the summary.
The desalination calculation reports minimum cost and benefit ratio eta=5.889 under epsilon=5.
Hai has the largest watershed pollution-control demand; Beijing receives higher city control priority than Datong.
Ningxia, Tibet, and Xinjiang have the largest beta values and therefore the most room for water-saving improvement.
AHP consistency ratio is reported below 0.1 for the test matrix and total sequencing.
The strategy table gives example economic, physical, environmental, other-impact, and quality scores for four projects.
The government paper recommends Yangtze-to-Yellow, Huai, and Hai transfer, southwest-to-northwest transfer, southeast-to-Pearl transfer, local storage, and early pollution control.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: The summary states the complete five-model ladder and the 2013-2025 leadership objective before details.

weaknesses.summary: Function fitting uses a short historical window for a thirteen-year forecast, so extrapolation uncertainty is not quantified.
The Verhulst table reports 6770.1 for 2025 while adjacent prose reports 7039; the source conflict is preserved.
The paper calls the forecast a Verhulst model, but the printed whitened equation has the linear GM form dX(1)/dt+aX(1)=b rather than a logistic quadratic term.
Reservoir cost, capacity, threshold, and benefit constants are not fully defined in the text extraction.
The province classification tables show Shanxi twice with different values, suggesting an unresolved Shanxi/Shaanxi label confusion.
A reservoir results table is split across physical pages 18-19, separating part of the header and body and requiring cross-page reconstruction.
Provincial coordinates, route-data provenance, and complete edge weights are not supplied for independent MST reproduction.
The printed transfer objective minimizes eta, while the Beijing example selects the maximum actual benefit; the optimization direction is internally inconsistent.
Desalination exponents and units are partially glyph-corrupted, and construction/maintenance calibration is absent.
Pollution-control gradient notation and COD source data are incomplete, limiting numeric reproduction.
The pollution interference exponent drifts between e^{-(j-k)} in prose and e^{-(j-i)} in the displayed accumulation formula.
The pollution-cost notation shifts from E_ij in the printed definition to E_kj in the later benefit ratios without an explicit index reconciliation.
The beta classification uses fixed bands without uncertainty or causal evidence that lower beta alone reduces pressure.
AHP consistency is reported, but eigenvector calculations and matrix provenance are not published.
AHP and neural evaluation provide only a small set of example strategy rows, which is insufficient for reproducible training, validation, or generalization.
The source's strengths and weaknesses are concise and do not quantify forecast, transfer, or evaluation uncertainty.
The position paper says 2015 while the body strategy horizon is 2013-2025; timing should be reconciled.
Appendix code names external text files and has no frozen environment, run log, assertions, or raw output archive.
Physical page 43 contains only a one-line MATLAB legend continuation and a large blank area, so it is retained as an appendix continuation rather than a substantive new section.
A persistent diagonal www.madio.net/Chinese watermark crosses all rendered pages and degrades some fine labels without preventing full-page review.
